_about: Pass 96 (lane LOOP, AI-01 / AI-08): the fixed questions every visual evaluator is asked, by id. tools/vision_eval.py reads them (rubric_text). A rubric is fixed text: no look note, job title, recipe word or file name ever goes into it (the label leak measured in pass 95: a model told the verdict by the file names scored 16/16, blind 10/16). The two legacy rubrics keep a placeholder their callers fill as before (gen_art.qa's subject, the Frames button's noun: those are the stills gate and a hand button, not the loop's evaluator); the `_blind` rubrics are the loop's and carry nothing about the asset. `fields` says which answer keys become findings items and when a value is a failure (bad_when); `record` keeps a value without a verdict (a count: no evaluator measured counts limbs reliably, D3); `per` is image (one call per picture) or sheet (one call for one contact sheet).

still_gate.text: You are checking a generated video game asset. Answer ONLY with one JSON object, no prose, with keys: subjects (integer, how many separate characters or objects are shown), background ("flat" if the background is a single flat color, otherwise "scene"), ground (true if a floor, ground plane, grass or a cast shadow is drawn under the subject), text (true if any letters, numbers or a watermark appear), cropped (true if part of the main subject is cut off by the image border), legs (true if the subject's legs and feet are both completely visible and drawn, false if any limb is missing or cut off), view ("front" if the main subject's face or front is towards the viewer, "back" if it is seen from behind with no face visible, "side" for a profile, else "other"), matches (true if the image clearly shows: {subject}).

subjects.rule: how many subjects the model counted

background.rule: the background must be one flat colour

cropped.rule: the subject must not be cut by the border

legs.rule: the legs and feet must be drawn whole

matches.rule: the picture must show the subject asked for

still_gate.note: gen_art.qa's question, kept word for word (the stills gate; its problems list is computed by gen_art.qa itself)

frame_ask.text: You are checking one frame of a 2D game sprite animation of {noun}. Answer ONLY with one JSON object, no prose, with keys: limbs (integer: how many legs or arms you can count), broken (true if a limb, the head or the body is cut, detached, smeared, doubled or missing), ghost (true if a faint or see-through duplicate of a part is visible), colour (true if a patch has a colour the rest of the figure lacks), note (a few words on what looks wrong, or "fine").

limbs.rule: limbs counted (a count no local eye does reliably: a hint, not a verdict)

broken.rule: a limb, the head or the body cut, detached, smeared, doubled or missing

ghost.rule: a faint or see-through duplicate of a part

colour.rule: a patch of a colour the rest of the figure lacks

frame_ask.note: the Frames view's Ask button, kept word for word (frames_io.ASK)

frame_blind.text: You are checking one frame of a 2D game sprite animation: one figure on a plain grey background. Answer ONLY with one JSON object, no prose, with keys: legs (integer: how many legs you can count), arms (integer: how many arms), broken (true if a limb, the head or the body is cut, detached, smeared, doubled or missing), ghost (true if a faint or see-through duplicate of a part is visible), face ("ok" if a face is drawn where the head is, "missing" if the head has no face at all, "wrong" if the face is a skull, doubled, or on the back of the head, "away" if the head is turned away from the viewer), smear (true if a part of the figure is blurred into streaks), colour (true if a patch has a colour the rest of the figure lacks), note (a few words on what looks wrong, or "fine").

legs.rule: legs counted (recorded, never a verdict: no evaluator measured counts them reliably)

broken.rule: a limb, the head or the body cut, detached, smeared, doubled or missing

ghost.rule: a faint or see-through duplicate of a part

face.rule: a face drawn where the head is (or the head turned away)

colour.rule: a patch of a colour the rest of the figure lacks

still_blind.text: You are checking one still painting of a video game character or creature on a flat background. Answer ONLY with one JSON object, no prose, with keys: subjects (integer: how many separate figures are shown), legs (integer: how many legs you can count), arms (integer), broken (true if a limb, the head or the body is cut, detached, smeared, doubled or missing), ghost (true if a faint or see-through duplicate of a part is visible), face ("ok" if a face is drawn where the head is, "missing" if the head has no face at all, "wrong" if the face is a skull, doubled, or on the back of the head, "away" if the head is turned away from the viewer), smear (true if a part is blurred into streaks), text (true if any letters, numbers or a watermark appear), note (a few words on what looks wrong, or "fine").

broken.rule: a limb, the head or the body cut, detached, smeared, doubled or missing

ghost.rule: a faint or see-through duplicate of a part

face.rule: a face drawn where the head is (or the head turned away)

still_blind.note: the loop's still rubric (tier 1 on a painting): hint-free

sheet_blind.text: This is a numbered contact sheet of frames from 2D game sprite animations. Each cell shows one frame with its number at the top left; the cells of one row belong to one animation. Answer ONLY with one JSON object, no prose, of the form {"cells": [{"n": <number>, "ok": true or false, "why": "a few words"}]} listing EVERY cell. ok is false only when that frame itself looks broken: a cut, detached, doubled, missing or smeared limb, head or body; a faint ghost duplicate of a part; a wrong or missing face; a patch of a foreign colour. Do not compare drawing styles between rows, and do not mark a frame for its pose.

cells.rule: the cloud eye's verdict on this cell of the decision sheet

sheet_blind.note: the loop's contact-sheet rubric (tier 2): one call per decision point

sheet_agy.text: This is a numbered contact sheet of frames from 2D game sprite animations of one character or creature. Each cell shows one frame on grey with its number in a black box at the top left; the cells may come from different animations and views. Judge every cell on its own. Answer ONLY with one JSON object, no prose, of the form {"cells": [{"n": <number>, "ok": true or false, "legs": <integer: how many legs you can count>, "ghost": true or false, "smear": true or false, "face": "ok" or "missing" or "wrong" or "away", "why": "a few words"}]} listing EVERY numbered cell. ok is false only when that frame itself looks broken: a cut, detached, doubled, extra, missing or smeared limb, head or body; a faint or see-through ghost duplicate of a part; a wrong or missing face; a patch of a foreign colour. ghost is true when a faint or see-through duplicate of a part is visible; smear is true when a part is blurred into streaks. Do not mark a frame for its pose or its drawing style.

cells.rule: Gemini's verdict on this cell of its contact sheet (a hint, not a verdict)

sheet_agy.note: pass 98 (lane GEMINI): Gemini through the Antigravity CLI on a numbered contact sheet of up to 16 frames (tier 2, Check / Ask Gemini); legs, ghost, smear and face come back per cell for the badges; a leg count alone never drives a repair (the bench: legs 2/11)
